analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call, 18 Nov 2026
key_insights: Tech led US equity futures pre-market on 11/18 (SPX +40bps, NDX +90bps, RTY unch, UST 10yr -0.5bps at 5.10%, WTI -95bps at $85.20) after NVDA's EPS (+3% pre-market) gave initial relief.

NVDA raised its CY27 sales growth guide to 75% from 70%. It reiterated its commitment to financial guarantees and commitments for partners and customers including neoclouds, which will continue in a disciplined and selective manner. Management said capital return (buyback and dividend) remains a major priority.
The AI complex opened better bid: DRAM +3%, SMH +2.3%, NBIS +6%, CRWV +4%, HUT +3%, IREN +5%, Samsung +2.4%, SK Hynix +4.3% pre-market.

GIR is Buy rated on NVDA, citing favorable risk/reward despite risks from the management transition and ongoing investigations. It expects the stock to hold its gains, with investor positioning neutral-to-negative per its conversations.
NVDA intends to return all excess cash to shareholders, with the ~$227bn remaining buyback authorization to be executed before the end of CY27.
Prime Insights: Global Fundamental L/S managers are -0.2% in November MTD (+8.9% YTD as of Nov 16). Systematic L/S is +1.1% MTD. TMT L/S funds are -4.5% MTD and Asia L/S funds -1.4% MTD.

Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities in November, with long and short sales at about 3 to 1. Single stocks were net sold in 7 of the last 8 weeks. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 7.6 pts MTD to 41.6%, a 5-year low and below Liberation Day lows. Gross leverage fell 4.4 pts to 206.3%.
GS says the equity market could set up for a tactical rally in the near term after persistent de-grossing and heavy net selling, as seasonality and technicals become friendlier.

Global Info Tech selling over the trailing 6 weeks is the fastest in a decade (-4.4 z score), led by Semis and Semi Equip. The global Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.79 versus a YTD peak of 2.9. US Semis net exposure fell below US Software net exposure for the first time since the start of 2026.

Industrials is the second most net sold US sector MTD, with net exposure at its lowest in more than two years. Consumer Staples is among the most net sold sectors. Hedge funds have cut US Health Care risk for 9 consecutive weeks.
Medium-term momentum factor exposure is on track to fall for a 6th straight month to the lowest since Dec 2022. Value factor exposure rose sharply to 5-year highs amid increased stagflation concerns.

Systematic macro estimate: global equity length cut from about $410bn three months ago to $290bn. CTAs sold about $80bn and risk parity plus vol-control about $25bn. About 75% of global short-trend signals are negative and 50% of medium-trend. S&P short and medium trend levels are around 7650 and 7550.

GS TMT desk (Callahan): NDX fell about 135 bps on 11/17 and retested its 11/5 intraday lows. The S&P 500 broke below its 200-dma for the first time since April, and defensives also traded lower. VIX moved through 26. ETFs were about 36% of the tape.

Semis are about 35% off highs, with all 30 SOX members down in 2H CY26. The desk said forward growth-rate debate (2028+) looks like investors inferring capex/GW growth from stock prices rather than bottoms-up revisions.

Flows on 11/17: floor activity was 3 out of 10. Asset managers were net sellers, led by large cap tech, and hedge fund flows were balanced. NKE finished -6% (from +3%) after its investor day as investors were skeptical of the 2031 guide.
2026 is on track for the most 10-year closes above 5% since 2007.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR is Buy on NVDA, expects the stock to hold gains after a solid quarter, with CY27 growth guide raised to 75% and neutral-to-negative positioning. GS also sees a possible tactical rally after record de-grossing and friendlier seasonality and technicals.
